summary: This article explains how the sun moves Earth's water through evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection, and why the water cycle matters in a dry country like Saudi Arabia.
introduce: Read the title “The Water Cycle” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: water that has turned into a gas you cannot see
to change from a gas into a liquid when cooled
water that falls from clouds, such as rain, snow, or hail

challengeTerms.def: the release of water vapor from plants through small openings in their leaves
an underground layer of rock or sand that holds water
when a gas cools and turns back into drops of liquid

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that saving water is important even in a country that can make fresh water from the sea? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Saudi Arabia gets very little rain.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review vapor, condense, and precipitation, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses transpiration, aquifer, and condensation to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
